reader.requirement: At 1985 the compiler must refuse a second USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION/ERROR PROCEDURE ON OUTPUT, or a second ON EXTEND, in the declaratives of one Procedure Division, while accepting OUTPUT and EXTEND once each and the same phrase again in a separate (contained) program's Procedure Division.

reader.edition-search: The _useModes register check in DeclBindUse takes no edition input (read it); the register is per ProcedureTableBuilder, i.e. per bound unit, so per Procedure Division.

reader.notes: The repeat check is the same code at 85 and 2023 (sr6outout gives the same COBOL0897 at --std 2023). The diagnostic text cites §2023:14.9.49.3 SR7 even at --std 85; the rule is enforced, only the message's citation names the later edition.

refuter.evidence: I attacked the 1985-only GLOBAL phrase (§1985 IPC USE [GLOBAL]) and the scope of 'a given Procedure Division'. r6globdup.cob: USE GLOBAL ... ON EXTEND plus USE ... ON EXTEND in one Procedure Division was refused with COBOL0897 (correct: EXTEND is specified twice). r6glob.cob: USE GLOBAL ON OUTPUT in the outer program and USE ON OUTPUT in a contained program compiled. Its output was OUTER 41 / INNER 41 / OUTER 41: the inner program's own USE ran, and a contained program with no USE reached the outer GLOBAL one. r6sep.cob: two separately compiled programs in one source, each with USE ON EXTEND, compiled and ran (A 41 / B 41). The register is per Procedure Division as SR6 says. The diagnostic cites §2023:14.9.49.3 SR7 even at --std 85; the reader already noted this, and it is a message-citation issue only. cite: OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.3 SR6  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR6.
